transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for having me. Is this chair okay? Okay, great, thank you. 

Um, well, honestly, I almost didn't come in because things are generally going really great at work, you know? I definitely don't want to make a big deal out of nothing. But... I guess for the past year or so, I've just been noticing that the smallest little things kind of pull me off whatever I'm doing before I can really stop it. 

Like, just a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office door... or even just a random thought popping into my head about my in-laws. It's nothing crazy, just a little annoying. I figure that's a pretty normal thing when you're running a business and have a lot on your plate, right? I just wanted to run it by you and make sure I'm doing everything I can to stay on top of things, if that makes sense?
Thinking back, would you say you've always been someone who's easily distracted, even back in school or earlier jobs, or is this level of distractibility something new that started around a year ago?

Well, um... I guess if I really look back, it's probably not completely new. I've always had a lot of energy, which honestly has been a huge asset for building my business, you know? 

But, yeah, back when I was a kid in school... I suppose I was always a bit of a handful. Nothing bad! Just, you know, very enthusiastic? I remember teachers were always moving my seat around because I guess I talked a little too much, or I'd just get up without asking first. And I had this habit of kind of... blurting things out before they even finished asking the question. I just got so eager to participate, I think. 

That's pretty typical kid stuff though, right? I mean, a lot of kids are just a little extra talkative like that, wouldn't you say?

When you get distracted by things like a phone buzz or a stray thought, is it usually because you're caught up in worrying about something, or does it happen even when you're not feeling worried at all?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm worried at all. Honestly, I'm... I'm a pretty positive guy, you know? Things are going really great with the business, so it's definitely not an anxiety thing. 

I can be in a fantastic mood, totally relaxed, not a care in the world, and... I don't know, my brain just kind of hops onto the next shiny thing anyway. Like, I'll just be sitting there feeling good, and a stray thought about a new project will just pop in and totally take over whatever I was actually supposed to be doing. 

I think I just have a really active mind, which is pretty common for guys running their own companies, right? It's definitely not because I'm sitting around stressing out or anything like that, I promise you that. Does that make sense?

Has this distractibility actually caused any real problems for you—like mistakes at work, missed deadlines, or friction with employees or family—or is it more just an occasional annoyance that doesn't really affect your outcomes?

Well, um... I mean, I'm definitely still keeping up with everything overall. The business is doing great, like I said. But, I guess... well, it has caused a few little hiccups here and there. Nothing I can't handle! 

But, you know, my wife has been getting a little frustrated with me lately. She feels like I'm not fully present when we're trying to figure out family plans, or I'll kind of zone out when she's talking. And at work... I try really hard to be a good mentor to my guys, but I think they get a little annoyed when I cut them off in meetings or lose track of what we were just talking about. It's just that I get so excited about the next step, you know? 

I really don't want them thinking I don't care, because I do, immensely. It's just... starting to cost me a little bit of trust at home, and maybe some patience from my team. But that's just something I need to work on being more mindful of, right? Everyone has things they can improve on, wouldn't you say?
These days, do you still notice things like feeling restless or fidgety, having trouble sitting still in meetings, or finding yourself talking more than others around you?

Well, um... I guess I do still have a lot of physical energy. I wouldn't call it restless, exactly. More just... active? I like to keep moving. 

But, yeah, in meetings... I suppose I do have a hard time just sitting totally frozen, you know? I might be, like, bouncing my knee a little bit under the table, or I'll catch myself clicking a pen, or just kind of shifting around in my chair. It's really just my way of staying engaged and keeping the blood flowing, I think! 

Although... I have noticed recently that some of the guys have started giving me these looks when I do it. Like they think I'm trying to rush them along or something? Which is awful, because I'm really trying my best to listen to them. I just process things better when I'm moving a little bit. 

That's not too unusual, though, is it? I mean, a lot of successful people are high-energy like that, right? I'm hoping it's just a sign of a strong work ethic, wouldn't you agree?
